claims.text: As-deposited nanoscale FeMnNiGeSi-type films or nanoribbons have high residual interface stresses.
As-deposited nanoscale FeMnNiGeSi-type films or nanoribbons contain a dense network of defects.
Annealing at approximately 400°C for 1 hour in argon will relieve built-in stresses.
The proposed annealing treatment will promote microstructural relaxation without causing grain growth or phase segregation.
Post-deposition annealing will reduce defect density in the nanoscale alloy.
Defects in the as-deposited alloy act as domain-wall pinning centers.
Reduced residual stress and defect density will reduce magnetic domain-wall pinning.
Reduced domain-wall pinning will enhance magnetic domain mobility.
Annealing-induced microstructural relaxation will improve thermal conduction across the thin film or nanoribbon.
Enhanced domain mobility and improved thermal conduction will produce a stronger magnetocaloric response under low applied fields.
Enhanced domain mobility will reduce magnetic hysteresis under low applied fields.
Annealed samples will exhibit a larger magnetic entropy change or adiabatic temperature change than as-deposited controls.
Annealed samples will exhibit less magnetic hysteresis than as-deposited controls.
The as-deposited baseline has significant magnetocaloric hysteresis caused by domain-wall pinning.
Limited thermal conduction in the nanoscale geometry contributes to the baseline hysteresis.
The proposed effect applies near 300 K and at applied magnetic fields below 0.5 T.
The usable cycling frequency is constrained by heat-transfer limitations.
Annealing conditions that cause phase segregation or excessive grain growth fall outside the proposed operating window.
Failure to obtain a statistically significant magnetocaloric improvement or hysteresis reduction relative to the as-deposited control would falsify the hypothesis.
